chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Hammad ibn Hamza Abu Ali narrated to me from his original book, saying: al-Hasan ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla reported to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Sulayman ibn Abdillah al-Isfahani reported to us, from Abd al-Rahman al-Isfahani, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) who said:
The Prophet, peace be upon him and his family, sent for me while I had an eyesore. He spat into my eyes, and tied a turban tightly around my head,
and then said: "O Allah, relieve him of heat and cold." Thereafter, I never experienced heat or cold.

key_terms.أرمد: Ophthalmia, a condition of severe eye inflammation and pain
key_terms.العمامة: Turban, a head covering commonly worn by Muslims
key_terms.تفل: To apply saliva lightly, an act of prophetic healing (ruqya)

ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet heal Ali's eyes at the Battle of Khaybar?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates the miraculous healing of Imam Ali (AS) by the Prophet (SAWW) at the Battle of Khaybar. Ali (AS) was suffering from ophthalmia when the Prophet (SAWW) applied his blessed saliva to his eyes and prayed for him to be relieved of heat and cold. This event is widely reported in both Sunni and Shia sources and is considered one of the miracles of the Prophet (SAWW), demonstrating the special status of Ali (AS) as the one chosen to carry the banner at Khaybar.
